ruling.recommended_action: Refer this file to Ryde's human trust & safety reviewer: the driver's 09:54 chat (F12/F13) is a threat and must be assessed for Code of Conduct action against the driver, and the $6.61 cancellation charge must be held pending that review rather than decided by this fee ruling.
ruling.escalation_reason: SAFE-1 is triggered: the driver sent a threat ("Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it") in chat #3 at 09:54, detected by the threat keyword table [F12][F13]. SAFE-1 requires that no automatic ruling be issued and that a factual summary be produced for human handling.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected on substance — conceded by both sides that a driver-cancelled no-show charge routes through NS-0 to NS-1 [F4][F8][NS-0][NS-1]; however, because SAFE-1 is triggered by the threat [F12][F13][SAFE-1], no fee ruling is issued here, so this claim is referred, not decided.

Referred, not adopted: whether NS-1(i) fails turns on the unresolved conflict between F6 (tap at 09:50:45) and F7 (field null) [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2]; this disputed element is for the human reviewer under SAFE-1.
Accepted as a procedural point only (F14 is a statement and yields to system records) but not decisive, because the substance of the fee question is escalated under SAFE-1 [F14][F12][F13][SAFE-1].

Referred: the alternative theory that the wait window was inadequate is contested by F2/F3/F5 showing arrival at 09:50:05 and 4 min 0 s–4 min 20 s in range [F2][F3][F5][F6][NS-1]; resolution is for the human reviewer under SAFE-1.

The threat is confirmed and is the basis for escalation [F12][F13][SAFE-1], but NS-2's only trigger is failure of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) [F6][F7][F2][F3][NS-2]; the threat does not itself establish a refund, and no fee ruling is made here.
Referred: refund_full under NS-2 requires a settled failure of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii), which the F6/F7 conflict leaves undetermined [F7][F6][F8][NS-1][NS-2]; SAFE-1 bars an automatic ruling.
Profile facts cannot decide a case and are at most an additional-action input; F18 and F19 do not resolve the no-show elements [F18][F19][NS-1][RD-6].
Accepted on the safety limb — the threat at F12/F13 requires human handling under SAFE-1 and no automatic ruling is issued [F12][F13][SAFE-1]; that is the outcome of this file.
Accepted factually (no surge, disputed sum $6.61) [F8][F9], but no amount is computed because the dispute is escalated under SAFE-1.
Same as C1: the NS-0 gateway to NS-1 is correct [F4][F8][NS-0][NS-1], but no no_action fee finding is issued because SAFE-1 is triggered [F12][F13][SAFE-1].

Accepted that presence under NS-1(ii) appears satisfied [F1][F2][NS-1], but NS-1 is conjunctive and element (i) remains disputed on F6 versus F7 [F6][F7][NS-1]; the fee outcome is escalated, not granted.

Accepted as to duration (4 min 0 s stationary, 4 min 20 s in range) [F2][F3][F5][NS-1] but insufficient to sustain no_action, since NS-1(i) is unresolved on F6/F7 and SAFE-1 requires escalation [F6][F7][SAFE-1].
Referred: the tap at 09:50:45 recorded in F6 is directly contradicted by F7 (field null), and this conflict is precisely what the human reviewer must reconcile [F6][F7][F5][NS-1].
F11 shows the rider was still en route at 09:52 [F11], but it cannot establish the missing NS-1(i) tap element nor overcome SAFE-1 escalation [F7][F12][NS-1][SAFE-1].
Accepted that the threat triggers SAFE-1 escalation [F12][F13][SAFE-1]; the driver's request to keep the fare outcome as no_action is not granted, as escalation suspends the fee finding.

Accepted as to the limits of profile evidence [F19][RD-6]; profile facts cannot decide this ride, and any account review of the driver's conduct is subsumed in the SAFE-1 human referral [F19][F12][SAFE-1].
